sentences.text: "Briefly stated, Injured Uday, son of Sanjeev Kumar, is a 4th-year B.A. LL.B. student at Kurukshetra University (KUK) and resides in Room No. B-46 of Tagore Hostel.

It is alleged that on the intervening night of 26/27.05.2025, around 12:45-1:00 A.M.,
he, along with his friend Amandeep, a 2nd-year LL.B. student, proceeded on a Bullet motorcycle bearing registration number HR- 02AY-1664 to get food outside the University premises.

During this time, Amandeep received a phone call from their friend Gurnam, a 1 of 7 CRM-M-48270-2025 resident of Amupur, District Karnal,
informing them that another friend of Rahul was being harassed by someone in the hostel and that a motorcycle was required to settle the matter.
Accordingly, Uday and Amandeep reached outside Devi Lal Hostel within five minutes, where they found Rahul and Rohit, who already had a motorcycle.
Subsequently, all five persons went to the first floor of Bhim Hostel, to the room where the alleged miscreants were believed to be staying.
However, the room was locked.

They then came down to the ground floor, where they found an open room occupied by 6-7 boys from the PHSO group, including Manish Ramgarhia, Krish Jat, Robin Paiga, and Sachin Dhillo,
among others.
The group appeared to be intoxicated and was creating a disturbance.
Upon seeing Uday and Gurnam, the PHSO members began hurling abuses.
It is noted that members of the PHSO group had previously assaulted Gurnam Singh a few days prior, though a compromise had reportedly been reached.
Uday and his companions requested them to stop the abusive behavior.
However, due to the deteriorating situation, Uday left the spot.
Gurnam and Rohit also returned to Devi Lal Hostel.
Due to the heat, Uday, along with Amandeep and Rahul, proceeded to Gujjar Dharamshala, where they had already booked a room.
Meanwhile, when the complainant and Rahul were leaving Devi Lal Hostel, a group of 15-16 masked individuals allegedly led by Manish Ramgarhia, who was unmasked, approached them from Narhari Hostel.
They were armed with gandasis and dandas and assaulted the complainant party.
Uday stopped his motorcycle inside Devi Lal Hostel.
Amandeep and Rahul, who were pillion riders, dismounted and ran toward the hostel stairs to save themselves.
Uday also abandoned his motorcycle and ran but slipped due to rainwater on the ground and because he was wearing bathroom slippers.
It had rained a day or two earlier, making the area slippery.
Thereafter, Manish Ramgarhia attacked Uday's left leg and knee with a gandasi.
Robin Paiga struck his right leg with a gandasi, while Krish Jat, Sachin Dhillo, and 8-10 unidentified accomplices attacked his arms and legs with dandas.
During the assault, they shouted threats such as, "Today, you are slashed; next will be your friend Gurnam."
Uday identified the attackers by their appearance and voices, though he could not identify the remaining assailants.

Upon hearing the noise, Uday's friends rushed to the spot,
prompting the attackers to flee while issuing further threats.
2 of 7 CRM-M-48270-2025 Uday was taken to LNJP Hospital, Kurukshetra by Gurnam and Amandeep.

He was then referred to Kalpana Chawla Medical College,
Karnal, but due to safety concerns, his family had him admitted to Singhu Hospital,
Jagadhri (Yamunanagar), where his statement was recorded, resulting in the registration of the present FIR."

sentences.text: the alleged criminal.1In deciding bail applications
an important factor which should certainly be taken into consideration by the Court is the delay in concluding the trial.--Often
this takes several years, and if the accused is denied bail but is ultimately acquitted,
who will restore so many years of his life spent in custody?
--Is Article 21 of the Constitution, which is the most basic of all the fundamental rights in our Constitution, not violated in such a case?
--Of course this is not the only factor, but it is certainly one of the important factors in deciding whether to grant bail.2
Personal liberty is a very precious fundamental right and it should be curtailed only when it becomes imperative according to the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.3

Personal liberty deprived when bail is refused, is too precious a value of our constitutional system recognised under Art. 21 that the curial power to negate it is a great trust exercisable, not casually, but judicially with lively concern for the cost to the individual and the community.4
When the undertrial prisoners are detained in jail custody to an indefinite period, Article 21 of the Constitution is violated.5 11.

Given the above, the penal provisions invoked viz-a-viz pre-trial custody, coupled with the primafacie analysis of the nature of allegations and the other factors peculiar to this case, there would be no justifiability for further pre-trial incarceration at this stage.

12. Without commenting on the case's merits, in the facts and circumstances peculiar to this case,
and for the reasons mentioned above, the petitioner makes a case for bail.
This order shall come into force from the time it is uploaded on this Court's official webpage.

13. with or without sureties, with a maximum bond amount not to exceed INR 10,000.
